# isObjectLike

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is object-like.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isObjectLike() — Checks whether a value is object-like. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.0.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isObjectLike(value: unknown): value is object;
```

Everything `isObject` accepts, plus functions: the question it answers is whether properties can be read off the value at all.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is object-like; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `object` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isObjectLike({}); // => true
isObjectLike([]); // => true
isObjectLike(function () {}); // => true
isObjectLike(null); // => false
isObjectLike("abc"); // => false
isObjectLike(1); // => false
```
